Subject: Re: RFP Q: Retention windows, export formats & nearline access SLA

Grant / team —

Thanks for the questions. I put together a concise technical appendix below; happy to expand any section into an appendix table or provide command samples. See also the attached retention matrix (CSV) and a sample manifest.

Summary (short):
- Hosted (Redwood API): Primary live store: 90 days rolling for raw request logs and model inference traces. Beyond 90d, audit records are tiered to compressed archive (immutable) for up to 7 years on request.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): Customer retains primary copies for 180 days by default; archival to immutable storage configurable up to 7 years.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Retention policy is customer-configurable per deployment; Redwood supports the retention tooling and export mechanisms but does not hold archived copies unless contracted.

Detailed export and access options:
- Supported export formats: NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) following our audit schema v1, Apache Parquet (columnar) with Avro schema mapping, and gzipped JSON Lines (.jsonl.gz). Each export includes a manifest.json with: file list, SHA256 checksums, schema version, and record counts.
- Slicing: Exports can be sliced by time range, user_id, request_id, or model_version. We also support predicate-based slices (e.g., error_code != 0 AND model_version = "v2.1").
- Nearline access: For data older than 90 days (hosted) we provide two options:
  * On-demand slice export (requested via the Console or API) — delivery as presigned S3 bundle (see SLA below).
  * Read-only nearline query (preview) — customers with Dedicated or Private (or hosted with an add-on) can request a temporary read-only Athena/BigQuery compatible view for ad-hoc queries (retained for up to 72 hours).

SLA / turnaround (export requests):
- Standard export: RTO 48 hours for slices up to 1 TB (after request accepted).
- Expedited export: RTO 8 hours (subject to capacity and additional fee).
- Bulk archive handback (full-year delivery): RTO 5 business days (packaged/ship or S3 delivery).
- SLAs exclude Gov/holiday blackout days and may be impacted by egress rates; expedited lane negotiable in SOW.

Integrity & chain-of-custody:
- Every archive is delivered with a signed manifest listing SHA256 hashes for each file and a delivery signature.
- We support customer-provided KMS keys (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or HSM) for envelope encryption of produced archives.
- Transfer options: S3 presigned URLs (recommended), direct sFTP over TLS, or couriered encrypted drive for large bulk export.
- We log the export job lifecycle (requested, queued, packaged, delivered) and can provide the event trail as part of the export bundle.

Redaction & PII handling:
- Redaction-on-export: We support field-level redaction rules applied at packaging time. Redaction rules are declarative (JSONPath-like selectors) and applied to the exported files; redacted fields are replaced with deterministic tokens and a redaction map included in the manifest.
- On-demand pseudonymization: For workflows that require re-identification later, we offer reversible pseudonymization with customer-managed keys (audit for re-ID requests logged).

Operational notes & examples:
- Typical export workflow:
  1) Customer opens an export request via Console or API (include slice parameters).
  2) Request is accepted and assigned a job id (e.g., job-20260930-045).
  3) Packaging runs and outputs files + manifest to a customer-specified S3 bucket or Redwood staging bucket (presigned URL).
  4) Customer downloads and verifies SHA256 checksums; Redwood retains packaging logs for 90 days post-delivery.

- Size guidance: NDJSON is preferred for row-by-row audit analysis; Parquet reduces footprint for analytics by ~6-10x depending on schema.

Attachment: retention-matrix.csv — contains default retention durations and archival cost tiers per deployment and per data class (request logs, KV cache snapshots, model outputs).

If Tessera requires a shorter standard retention (e.g., 180 days hosted), we can adjust via contract. For exports requiring immediate legal hold, we typically onboard a preservation workflow (LegalOps integration) to lock affected records and prioritize packaging.

Happy to jump on a 30-minute call to walk through a live demo of an export job.

—
Laura Bennett
Principal Engineer, Platform
Redwood Inference

Grant —

Numbers & commercial notes from our side:
- Export pricing: standard export up to 1 TB is included once per contract year for Hosted customers on enterprise plans; additional exports billed at $0.15/GB packaged. Expedited lane has a fixed fee (example: $2,500 per expedited request) to cover priority packaging.
- SLA credits: For expedited export SLA misses (8h lane), we offer service credits (pro-rated) as a contract term; we can include a performance credit table in the SOW.
- Onboarding: If Tessera wants nearline query views (Athena-compatible), there is a one-time enablement fee; otherwise the API/Console export flow is available at no extra integration effort.

Next steps:
1) Confirm whether you want customer-managed KMS for exports — if yes, add that to the SOW.
2) If LegalOps wants the preservation workflow, we'll draft an MSA addendum that includes a 48-hour standard export commitment and pricing for expedited exports.

If helpful I can draft the SOW language and pricing table; Karthik / Laura, can you confirm the 48h / 8h SLAs above as reasonable to commit in the SOW?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
